questions.question: Some of the talas invented by _________ include Trimukhi, Panchamukhi, Saptamukhi and Navamukhi.
questions.questionHtml: Some of the talas invented by _________ include Trimukhi, Panchamukhi, Saptamukhi and Navamukhi.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is M. Balamuralikrishna.

Key Points

  • M. Balamuralikrishna was an Indian Carnatic vocalist, musician, multi-instrumentalist, playback singer, composer, and character actor.
  • He was known for his deep knowledge of both the theoretical and practical aspects of Carnatic music.
  • He invented new ragas as well as talas, including the ones mentioned: Trimukhi, Panchamukhi, Saptamukhi, and Navamukhi.
  • His contributions to Carnatic music earned him several prestigious awards, including the Padma Vibhushan and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

Additional Information

  • Carnatic Music
    • Carnatic music is a system of music commonly associated with the southern part of the Indian subcontinent, with its foundations in ancient Hindu traditions.
    • It is one of the two main subgenres of Indian classical music that evolved from ancient Hindu traditions, the other subgenre being Hindustani music.
    • The main emphasis in Carnatic music is on vocal music; most compositions are written to be sung, and even when played on instruments, they are meant to be performed in a singing style (known as gayaki).
  • Tala
    • Tala, literally meaning "clap," is the term used in Indian classical music to refer to musical meter, that is, any rhythmic beat or strike that measures musical time.
    • It is a series of beats that are cyclically repeated.
    • Talas can have different numbers of beats, and the cycle of beats is divided into sections called "angas," which can be of varying lengths.
  • Instruments Played by M. Balamuralikrishna
    • Besides being a renowned vocalist, M. Balamuralikrishna was proficient in playing the violin, viola, mridangam, and kanjira.
    • His multifaceted talent in playing various instruments added to his versatility and depth as a musician.

Additional Information

questions.question: Who among the following Indian musicians was a part of a band named 'Planet Drum' along with Mickey Hart, Sikiru Adepoju, and Giovanni Hidalgo, whose first album received the 1992 Grammy Award for Best World Music Album, which was the first Grammy in this category?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following Indian musicians was a part of a band named 'Planet Drum' along with Mickey Hart, Sikiru Adepoju, and Giovanni Hidalgo, whose first album received the 1992 Grammy Award for Best World Music Album, which was the first Grammy in this category?

    • The sitar is a plucked stringed instrument used in Hindustani classical music.
    • It has a long neck and a gourd-shaped body, with 18-20 strings including both playing and sympathetic strings.
    • Renowned sitar players include Ravi Shankar, Vilayat Khan, and Anoushka Shankar.
    • The sitar is known for its deep, resonant sound and is often used to play ragas, which are melodic frameworks for improvisation in Indian classical music.
  • Bansuri
    • The bansuri is an Indian flute made from a single hollow shaft of bamboo with six or seven finger holes.
    • It is traditionally used in Indian classical music and folk music.
    • Notable bansuri players include Hariprasad Chaurasia and Pannalal Ghosh.
  • Tabla
    • The tabla is a pair of twin hand drums from the Indian subcontinent, used in traditional, classical, popular, and religious music.
    • It consists of a small right-hand drum called the dayan and a larger left-hand drum called the bayan.
    • Famous tabla players include Zakir Hussain and Alla Rakha.
  • Sarangi
    • The sarangi is a bowed, short-necked string instrument from India, Nepal, and Pakistan.
    • It is used in Hindustani classical music and is known for its rich, resonant sound.
    • Prominent sarangi players include Ram Narayan and Sabri Khan.

questions.question: Which of the following is called the cyclic arrangement of time units in Hindustani Classical music?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is called the cyclic arrangement of time units in Hindustani Classical music?
questions.solution: Tala, in Hindustani Classical music, refers to the cyclic arrangement of time units that form the rhythmic framework of a musical composition. It helps musicians maintain tempo and structure, with various types like Teentaal, Ektaal, and Jhaptal, each having specific beat patterns. Tala is essential for both performance and composition, providing a foundation for melodies. Other terms include Jati, which classifies Ragas by notes; Alap, the introductory section of a Raga performance; and Raga, the melodic framework for improvisation and composition. Understanding Tala enhances the appreciation of Hindustani Classical music's complexity and beauty.

questions.question: Which of the following is a string instrument commonly featured in the folk music of Gujarat?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is a string instrument commonly featured in the folk music of Gujarat?
questions.solution: The Jantar is a string instrument commonly featured in the folk music of Gujarat. It is made from bamboo with strings stretched across a resonating box, producing sound when plucked. The Jantar is often used in traditional performances, especially in rural areas, to accompany singing or storytelling. It has a deep, resonant sound and is closely associated with tribal and nomadic communities. In contrast, the Bungal, Pava, and Turi are wind instruments used in Gujarat's folk traditions for ceremonial and festive occasions. The Bungal is a long, curved trumpet, the Pava is similar to a flute, and the Turi is a horn-like instrument.

questions.question: In Hindustani classical music, according to Vishnu Narayana Bhatkhande, how many thaats are the origins of ragas?
questions.questionHtml: In Hindustani classical music, according to Vishnu Narayana Bhatkhande, how many thaats are the origins of ragas?
questions.solution: The concept of Thaats in Hindustani classical music was systematized by Pandit Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande in the early 20th century, establishing 10 fundamental Thaats as the origins of ragas. Bhatkhande, who trained under Balakrishnabuwa Ichalkaranjikar and Ali Hussain Khan, founded Marris College of Music in Lucknow, later named Bhatkhande Music Institute. His Thaat system is often compared to the Melakarta system in Carnatic music, which has 72 parent scales.

questions.question: Which of the following is a folk song genre popular in parts of West Bengal, Assam and Bangladesh?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is a folk song genre popular in parts of West Bengal, Assam and Bangladesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bhawaiya.

Key Points

  • Bhawaiya is a major genre of folk song popular throughout the entire sub-Himalayan belt of northern West Bengal, western Assam and parts of Bangladesh.
  • Its origin is drawn from various theatrical and matriarchal ritual folk music traditions.
  • Bhawaiya has developed into a socially conscious yet lyrical song tradition that is a mainstay of the culture of the Rajbanshi, Koch and other communities of North Bengal.
  • Mostly written from the perspective of the woman.
  • Songs speak of love not socially mandated but arising unbidden between men and women thrown together by the vagaries of a marginalized socio-economic existence.
  • The woman in a bhawaiya song is often a loner, a young widow or a woman in the full bloom of youth who is yet to find a loving husband.

Additional Information

  • Rekham Pada
    • ​Rekham Pada is a folk dance popular in Arunachal Pradesh.
    • It is one of the main dance forms of the Nishi Tribe.
    • Both men and women participate in this dance.
    • Rekham Pada is accompanied by a song, which is sung normally in chorus.
    • The tribe members dance Rekham Pada during important rituals, during festivals, and also for recreation occasionally.
  • Chalo
    • ​The Chalo dance is part of Arunachal Pradesh's most awaited festival, called Chalo Loku.
    • This festival is a grand celebration in the state and takes place every year in October and November.
    • It is a celebration of the Nocte tribe.
    • The name “Chalo Loku” translates to paddy cultivation season in English.
  • Roppi
    • ​Roppi is one of the popular folk dances of Arunachal Pradesh.
    • It is mainly performed by the tribal group of the state.

questions.question: In which Gharana do singers perform the Khandhar Vani and Gauhar Vani?

questions.solution: The Darbhanga Gharana is renowned for its distinctive Dhrupad singing style, one of the oldest forms of North Indian classical music. This Gharana emphasizes clarity of notes, intricate rhythmic patterns, and powerful vocal delivery. It has significantly contributed to the preservation and propagation of Dhrupad music. Other notable Gharanas include the Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana, known for its vocal aesthetics and technical aptitude; Patiala Gharana, famous for Thumri and Khyal singing; Banaras Gharana, originating from Thumri singers of Benaras and Gaya; and Maihar Gharana, a school of Hindustani classical music.

questions.question: Which of the following instruments is played by Anokhelal Mishra?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following instruments is played by Anokhelal Mishra?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Tabla.

Key Points

  • Anokhelal Mishra was an Indian Tabla Artist who belonged to the Banaras Gharana of Hindustani classical music.
  • Anokhelal Learnt Tabla for about 15 years from Bhairow Prasad Mishra. Bhairow Prasad Mishra was a disciple of Bhagat-ji. Bhagat-Ji was a disciple of Ram Sahai, the founder of The Banaras-Baj (aka Banaras Gharana). 
  • He also spelled as AnokheLal Misra and commonly known as Pandit Anokhelalji​

Additional Information

  • Surbahar​ is an Indian player of Rudra Veena, Saraswati Veena, and Surbahar. He is unique in being a left-handed artist who has mastered all the three veenas of Indian classical music - the Rudra Veena, the Saraswati Veena, and the Surbahar.
  • Sarod is an adaptation of the Afghan rabab, which arrived in India during the 16th century. The modern form of the instrument was designed in the 19th century. It is one of the most important concert instruments in Hindustani music and is often accompanied by the tabla (drums) and tambura (drone lute).
  • Shehnai is a ​double-reed conical oboe of North India. The shehnai is made of wood, except for a flaring metal bell attached to the bottom of the instrument, and measures about 12–20 inches (30–50 cm) in length, with six to eight keyless finger holes along its body.

questions.question: Asghari Bai is primarily remembered for her contribution to which of the following genres of music?
questions.questionHtml: Asghari Bai is primarily remembered for her contribution to which of the following genres of music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dhrupad.

Key Points

  • Asghari Bai:-
    • She was an Indian Dhrupad singer.
    • She was one of the oldest and most respected exponents of this ancient form of Hindustani classical music.
    • She was also a woman in a male-dominated field, which made her achievements even more remarkable. 
    • Asgari Bai was known for her powerful and expressive voice, as well as her deep understanding of the Dhrupad tradition.
    • She was also a gifted teacher, and she mentored many young musicians over the years.
    • In recognition of her contributions to music, Asgari Bai was awarded numerous honors and awards, including the Padma Shri, the Tansen Samman, and the Shikhar Samman.
    • She was also featured in a documentary film, Asgari Bai (1998), which explores her life and work.
  • Dhrupad:-
    • It is a form of Hindustani classical music that originated in North India.
    • It is one of the oldest and most prestigious forms of Indian classical music, and is characterized by its slow tempo, complex rhythms, and intricate vocal ornamentation.

Additional Information

  • Carnatic music:-
    • It is a form of Indian classical music that originated in South India.
    • It is characterized by its complex rhythms and melodies, based on the classical Indian frameworks of talas and ragas.
  • Ghazal:-
    • It is a form of lyric poetry that originated in the Arabic world in the 7th century.
    • It is characterized by its unique rhyme scheme and thematic structure.

questions.question: Pandit Ananda Gopal Bandopadhyay was a _________ player of the Banaras gharana.
questions.questionHtml: Pandit Ananda Gopal Bandopadhyay was a _________ player of the Banaras gharana.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is tabla.

Key Points

  • Pandit Ananda Gopal Bandopadhyay was a tabla player of the Banaras gharana. 
    • Indian tabla player Ananda Gopal Bandopadhyay lived from April 28, 1942, to May 7, 2021.
    • His instructor Mahadev Prasad Mishra instructed him in the Banaras Gharana style.
    • Radha Gopal Bandopadhyay, his father, was an amateur singer.
    • Bandopadhyay has performed and recorded alone as well as partnered with a number of well-known vocalists.
    • He was a former professor at the ITC Sangeet Research Academy in Kolkata and a well-regarded performer for both Doordarshan and All India Radio.
    • He received the President's gold medal for taking first place in the All India Radio music competition in 1965.
    • He also received a gold medal from the Ethiopian Emperor in 1970, an award rarely bestowed upon foreigners.
    • He received the Sangeet Ratna Award from The Salt Lake Music Association in 2012.

Additional Information

  • Along with performing in India, he has also appeared in Boston, New York, San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Berlin's World Youth Festival.
  • Banaras Gharana 
    • Pandit Ram Sahai created the Banaras tabla gharana a little more than 200 years ago.
    • It is one of the six most popular ways to play the Indian tabla.
    • He went into solitude for six months during which he worked to create the Benares baj, or style, of playing the tabla.
    • This new tabla playing technique was developed with the idea that it would be adaptable enough to perform both solo and to accompany any style of music or dance.
